summary: An agentic research assistant that answers questions about ocean and climate research papers using hybrid retrieval, reranking, and citation-grounded generation. It also supports numerical queries over a structured oceanographic dataset.

images.caption: Answers with paper and page references

sections.title: The challenge
body: Scientific research often means searching across many papers, finding the passages that matter, and combining them with numbers from datasets.
This project explores an assistant that automates part of that workflow. It decides where to look, retrieves and ranks the evidence, and answers with references to its sources.

steps.title: Document ingestion
steps.text: Research PDFs are extracted and processed into text.

steps.title: Chunking
steps.text: Text is divided into overlapping chunks that keep paper and page metadata.

steps.title: Dense retrieval
steps.text: Sentence-transformer embeddings retrieve semantically relevant passages from ChromaDB.

steps.title: Keyword retrieval
steps.text: BM25 finds passages that match important terms in the query.

steps.title: Hybrid fusion
steps.text: Reciprocal Rank Fusion combines the dense and keyword rankings.

sections.title: Evaluation
sections.note: Measured on a set of 11 test cases. These results reflect the current evaluation set and test environment, and are not guarantees for arbitrary research questions or larger datasets.

sections.title: Research corpus and data
body: The corpus focuses on ocean science, ENSO dynamics, ocean prediction and sea-surface temperature modeling.

The data tool runs over a small sample dataset with date, latitude, longitude, depth, temperature and salinity fields. It demonstrates the data-querying workflow and is not a comprehensive observational dataset.

sections.title: What's next
items: Expand the research corpus and evaluate retrieval on a larger, more diverse set of questions.
Improve latency and measure the contribution of each pipeline stage.
Add more robust answer-quality and faithfulness evaluation.
Improve handling of conflicting evidence across papers.
Deploy the frontend and backend for public access.
Add user-facing source inspection and richer research workflows.
